You can use all parameters available for everyone plus these additional attributes
Get the last activity date for users with public profiles

assumptions: The full user list with emails, last activity and admin flag comes from the administrator version of GET /users, which the docs say is for GitLab Self-Managed and GitLab Dedicated. On GitLab.com a non-admin token only gets a limited list without emails or activity dates.

Self-managed customers have their own host (for example gitlab.example.com). The rules don't allow a fully variable host, so I set the base URL to https://gitlab.com/api/v4. Self-managed use would need the host changed.

Authentication: the docs only show a personal-style access token sent in the PRIVATE-TOKEN header. They don't say which token types or scopes are needed. I assumed an administrator token with read access (probably read_api or api). Prefer a service-account-style or non-personal token if the customer can create one.
The docs don't state a maximum page size. I used 100 per page, which is a sensible value but not confirmed here.

The docs mention keyset pagination for very large lists (50,000+ users). I used page-number pagination (page, per_page), which the docs also describe. Very large instances may need keyset pagination instead.
The list response is a plain JSON array at the top level. I used "$" to mean the root of the response, which the docs don't spell out.
The docs only show the state values 'active' and 'blocked'. The mappings for deactivated, banned, blocked_pending_approval and ldap_blocked come from general knowledge of GitLab, not this source.
Role is derived only from the is_admin flag (admin or member). Other roles, such as auditor, are not mapped.
User type (human, bot, service) is not mapped, because the admin list response doesn't include a clear bot field. Bots and service accounts may appear as ordinary members.

Activity: last_activity_on is a date only (no time of day), and is used as the last active date. last_sign_in_at is the fallback. The docs say these timestamps are updated by Git activity, logins, page visits and API use.
The docs don't say whether the admin list includes blocked and deactivated users by default. The wording 'By default it returns all users' suggests it does, and I added no filters.
Rate limits are not stated in the source, so they are left empty.
I did not set a plan requirement. The admin listing is only offered on Self-Managed and Dedicated, but it is available in the Free tier.
